speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth with the completion of another Southeast Asian Games and ASEAN Para Games, how does the Ministry support the post-Games and post-sports career plans of athletes, especially for those who went into full-time training to represent Singapore for these Games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Network also organises career-readiness workshops to guide our athletes, as well as networking opportunities with the corporate partners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They include former national athletes, such as shuttler Derek Wong, who has made a successful transition to a post-sport career with Deloitte, and current national athletes, such as netballer Charmaine Soh who is also with Deloitte, as well as archer Christina Gunawan and CP footballer Khairul Anwar who are employed with other spexBusiness partners such as KPMG and MCCY.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With more companies on board, we are able to support more athletes in their pursuit of sporting excellence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Besides the spexBusiness Network, there are also opportunities for athletes to pursue a career in their respective sports and continue to contribute to the sports' development after they have retired from competition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our increased funding support over the years for the development of sport − from the learn-to-play entry level to the high performance level − has enlarged the ecosystems of many sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This has created more employment opportunities for national athletes to work in the areas that they are passionate about and pass down their experience to the younger generation of athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Many of our former national athletes have led the way, such as former national swimmer Gary Tan, who is now the Head Coach of the National Training Centre for swimming, and former national shuttler Jiang Yanmei, who is now the Technical Manager of the Singapore Badminton Association (SBA) and Principal of the SBA Badminton Academy@ActiveSG.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first one is: our national athletes are great ambassadors of the sports for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Is there a structured process for them to take up permanent roles within ActiveSG?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And the second question: within the different schools, we have been trying to promote sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it is both in Institutes of Higher Learning as well as outside.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is really to provide more opportunities and options for our athletes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Some of them may like to pursue a career in coaching − that is available to them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The idea is to give the athletes options.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Some of them may like to stay in the sports that they are passionate about.
